source.english_context: Unit 16 Community, Neighbors, and Social Customs Goal: build a simple support network and understand friendly everyday behavior. Daily Life English Nice to meet you. I just moved in. Do you know where the library is? Could you recommend a local doctor? Thank you for your help. I appreciate it. Is there an English conversation group nearby? How do I get a library card? Are there any free activities this weekend? What time does the community center open? Would you like to join us for coffee? Could you please turn the music down? Is this parking space shared? How can I volunteer here? Do I need to sign up for this event? It was nice talking with you. Please let me know if you need anything. Vocabulary neighbor a person who lives near you library a public place with books, computers, and programs community center a place with local services and activities recommend say something is good or useful small talk short friendly conversation personal space comfortable distance between people library card a card used to borrow items from a library volunteer a person who helps without being paid event an organized activity or gathering sign up put your name on a list to join an activity invitation a message asking someone to join you shared space an area used by more than one person or group US Customs People often use small talk about weather, weekends, pets, or local places. A smile and "How are you?" can be a greeting, not a long question. Libraries and community centers can help with English, forms, computers, and local information. For a first conversation, introduce yourself and keep questions simple. Give the other person room to end the conversation politely. Ask before borrowing something or using another person's belongings. Agree on when and how you will return a borrowed item. If someone invites you to an event, confirm the time and place. Ask whether you should bring anything with you. When discussing a shared-space problem, describe the issue calmly and make a specific request instead of blaming a neighbor. Dialogue Student: Hi, I just moved in next door. Neighbor: Welcome to the building. Student: Thank you. Do you know when trash pickup is? Neighbor: Tuesday morning. Put bins outside Monday night. Student: That helps a lot. Where do the recycling bins go? Neighbor: Beside the blue sign near the back gate. Student: Is there a notice with the building rules? Neighbor: Yes. There is one in the lobby, next to the mailboxes. Student: Great. I will take a look. My name is Mina, by the way. Neighbor: Nice to meet you, Mina. I am Alex.

japanese_explanation.heading: 小さな会話が助けになる
points: 近所の人との短い挨拶は大切です。深い関係を作らなくても、困った時に質問しやすくなります。
How are you? は長い答えを求めていないことが多いです。Good, thanks. How about you? で十分です。
図書館やコミュニティセンターは、英語、パソコン、書類、地域情報の助けになることがあります。

existing_simplified_chinese.heading: 小对话也能带来帮助
points: 和邻居简单打招呼很有用。即使不是很亲近，以后遇到问题也更容易开口问。
How are you? 很多时候只是问候，不一定需要长回答。Good, thanks. How about you? 就够了。
图书馆和社区中心可能提供英语、电脑、表格和本地信息方面的帮助。

ko.heading: 작은 대화가 도움이 될 수 있습니다
points: 이웃과 짧게 인사하는 것이 중요합니다. 깊은 관계를 맺지 않더라도, 어려울 때 질문하기가 더 쉬워집니다.
"How are you?"는 긴 답변을 기대하지 않는 경우가 많습니다. "Good, thanks. How about you?"로 충분합니다.
도서관과 커뮤니티 센터는 영어, 컴퓨터, 서류 및 지역 정보와 관련하여 도움을 줄 수 있습니다.

es.heading: Las pequeñas conversaciones pueden ayudar
points: Saludar brevemente a los vecinos es importante. Aunque no se establezcan relaciones profundas, será más fácil hacer preguntas cuando se necesite ayuda.
A menudo, "How are you?" no busca una respuesta larga. "Good, thanks. How about you?" es suficiente.
Las bibliotecas y los centros comunitarios pueden ayudar con el inglés, las computadoras, los trámites y la información local.

pt-BR.heading: Pequenas conversas podem ajudar
points: Cumprimentar brevemente os vizinhos é importante. Mesmo que você não forme laços profundos, fica mais fácil fazer perguntas quando precisar de ajuda.
Muitas vezes, "How are you?" não espera uma resposta longa. "Good, thanks. How about you?" é suficiente.
Bibliotecas e centros comunitários podem ajudar com inglês, computadores, formulários e informações locais.

fr.heading: Les petites conversations peuvent être utiles
points: Saluer brièvement vos voisins est important. Même si vous n'établissez pas de relations profondes, il vous sera plus facile de poser des questions en cas de besoin.
La question "How are you?" ne demande souvent pas une longue réponse. "Good, thanks. How about you?" est suffisant.
Les bibliothèques et les centres communautaires peuvent vous aider avec l'anglais, les ordinateurs, les documents et les informations locales.

de.heading: Kleine Gespräche können hilfreich sein
points: Kurze Begrüßungen mit Nachbarn sind wichtig. Auch wenn Sie keine tiefen Beziehungen aufbauen, fällt es Ihnen leichter, Fragen zu stellen, wenn Sie Hilfe brauchen.
„How are you?“ verlangt oft keine lange Antwort. „Good, thanks. How about you?“ ist ausreichend.
Bibliotheken und Gemeindezentren können bei Englisch, Computern, Formularen und lokalen Informationen helfen.
